page: Vultr voc-s-1c-8gb-150s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring a single dedicated AMD EPYC vCPU clocked at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. Storage is provided via a local 150 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance placing in the top 10% and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 25%. However, due to the single-core constraint, multi-core benchmarks are limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth is average, with large-block read and write speeds reaching 40.43 GB/sec and 36.8 GB/sec.

This server offers high resource density for single-threaded tasks, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring dedicated CPU execution without the overhead of multi-core licensing. However, the single-core limitation results in poor performance for highly parallelized tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving. It is best suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, memory-intensive background workers, small-scale database operations, or basic text processing.
